omitted_tabs.reason: MySQL does not allow triggers on views.

gaps.reason: Native grants/revokes are separate provider operations. Embedding their diff in a view edit requires the cross-operation dispatch contract in Decision 9.

MySQL 9.7.0 Community accepts CREATE and ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW and stores them as definition metadata (SHOW CREATE VIEW reports BY ENGINE=UNKNOWN); physical materialization needs a supporting engine, and closed Enterprise execution is post beta.

fields.label: Database
fields.help: Database name as a single native identifier; the selected object supplies this identity during alteration.

fields.label: Column aliases
fields.help: Ordered names for the view's output columns; leave empty to use the query's own names.

fields.label: Definer user
fields.help: Supply both user and host when changing the definer.

notes: Ordinary and materialized view create/alter through mysql_views.compile_operation. ALTER restates the whole view; options the edit leaves out keep the view's current values from the inspected record (definition, declared aliases, algorithm, security, check option, definer). Round-tripped 2026-11-05 on the MySQL 9.7.0 demo (tools/tests/test_ui_descriptor_roundtrip_mysql.py): every field set, pre-filled on reopen, and single-option alters keep the rest; a materialized view stays materialized. Privileges stay separate grant/revoke operations (Decision 9 default).
